diffuseAlbedo.note: Lizard serpentine, Cornwall: dark green and red serpentine veined with white; no measured colour was read: a first value read from trade and museum photographs of the named material (as the Oxford University Museum's shafts show it).

refractiveIndex.source: Anthony, Bideaux, Bladh & Nichols, Handbook of Mineralogy, 'Lizardite' (Mineral Data Publishing, 2001, v1.2), Optical Properties: alpha 1.538-1.554, beta 1.546-1.560, gamma 1.546-1.560; name for the type locality, the Lizard complex, Cornwall; chemical analysis (1) and X-ray pattern from Kennack Cove. https://www.handbookofmineralogy.org/pdfs/lizardite.pdf
refractiveIndex.note: Checked against the PDF: the indices, the Kennack Cove analysis and the type-locality naming are all as stated. Corrected: the proposal gave the F0 values as 0.0468 and 0.0475. Recomputed, F0 is 0.0467 at 1.551 and 0.0479 at 1.56. The Handbook does not say the Lizard rock is mainly lizardite. That is an inference from the naming and the Kennack Cove analysis. It is reasonable, but it is not stated. Bastite, chrysotile and the hematite of the red variety are left out.
refractiveIndex.derivation: n = mean of the mid-range principal indices = (1.546 + 1.553 + 1.553) / 3 = 1.5507, rounded 1.551. F0 = ((n-1)/(n+1))^2 = 0.0467 (was 0.0479 at 1.56).

porosity.source: 'Decoding the nanoscale porosity in serpentinites from multidimensional electron microscopy and discrete element modelling', Contributions to Mineralogy and Petrology 178(11), published 17 Oct 2023, PMC11008076: in lizardite-dominated serpentinites, the average porosity of the FIB-SEM excavated volumes is 0.4 +/- 0.07 %, 0.7 +/- 0.08 % and 0.2 +/- 0.05 %; TEM foils average 1-3 %; nanopores are mostly under 10 nm, with some up to 100 nm. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11008076/
porosity.note: Corrected: the paper is from 2023 in Contrib. Mineral. Petrol. 178(11), not 2024. 0.005 lies inside the 0.002-0.007 FIB-SEM range. This is evidence for the rock type only. The samples are from ODP Leg 209 Site 1274 on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and the Roragen complex in Norway, not from the Lizard. The paper measures total nanoporosity and does not separate connected (open) porosity. Its models suggest the pores connect but warn that natural rock may be less connected. So as an open porosity this value is an upper-leaning estimate.

wettingDepth.note: The depth whose pores govern the face's look when wet.

grain.note: The finest structure the face shows at gallery distance.

bed.note: The coarsest structure the face shows: its bedding, veining or banding.

bedAspect.note: How much longer the structure runs along its bedding than across it.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the travertine's.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(albedo) across one face.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
